package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2019-7238) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server by sending a specially crafted HTTP request to an exposed REST API endpoint. While the package itself is not intentionally malicious, the vulnerability enables malicious exploitation, making unpatched versions highly dangerous in production environments due to the risk of full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: Upon receiving a specially crafted HTTP request to a vulnerable REST API endpoint
execution_context.file_location: Undisclosed internal Java class handling REST API requests (core server-side component)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read/write files as the Nexus process)
process_execution (to spawn or control system processes)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The vulnerable REST API endpoint processes attacker-controlled input without proper validation or sanitization, allowing the attacker to inject and execute arbitrary code on the server. The exploit is triggered when the server receives a maliciously crafted HTTP request targeting the vulnerable endpoint, resulting in execution of commands with the privileges of the Nexus Repository Manager process.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Java (server-side, exploit via HTTP request payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes untrusted user input in a REST API endpoint without adequate validation, enabling attackers to inject and execute arbitrary system commands on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The REST API endpoint fails to validate or sanitize user-supplied input, directly passing it to code execution routines. This allows attackers to craft HTTP requests that result in arbitrary command execution on the server, a hallmark of remote code execution vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal REST API endpoints should strictly validate and sanitize all user input, ensuring that no user-supplied data is ever executed as code or commands. Executing user input as code is a severe violation of secure coding practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate REST APIs may process user input for business logic, but should never interpret or execute user-supplied data as code or system commands. Any such behavior is highly abnormal and dangerous.
key_indicators: Arbitrary code or command execution triggered by HTTP request payloads
Lack of input validation or sanitization in REST API endpoint
Execution of system-level commands with Nexus Repository Manager process privileges
Ability to upload or modify files on the server via crafted requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies a publicly accessible instance of Nexus Repository Manager 3 running a version prior to 3.15.
Attacker crafts and sends a malicious HTTP request to the vulnerable REST API endpoint, exploiting the input validation flaw.
The server processes the malicious request, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the Nexus Repository Manager process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full system compromise, data exfiltration, installation of backdoors, or further lateral movement within the network

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process execution (e.g., shell, scripting engines) initiated by the Nexus Repository Manager process
Unusual outbound network connections from the repository server to external or untrusted IP addresses
Abnormal or malformed HTTP requests to REST API endpoints, especially those containing suspicious payloads or command injection patterns
Creation or modification of files in server directories not associated with normal repository operations
file_indicators: Unexpected files or scripts appearing in the server filesystem (e.g., web shells, binaries, or scripts in temporary or application directories)
Modifications to configuration or binary files outside of scheduled maintenance or upgrade cycles
Presence of files with suspicious names or extensions (e.g., .sh, .bat, .exe) in application or temp directories
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from the repository server to external IPs or domains not associated with normal repository operations
Inbound HTTP requests to REST API endpoints with atypical, malformed, or excessively long payloads
Repeated failed or anomalous authentication attempts to REST API endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the Nexus Repository Manager process for abnormal child process creation and unexpected command execution. Analyze HTTP access logs for suspicious or malformed requests to REST API endpoints, particularly those containing command injection patterns. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes or the appearance of new files in application and temporary directories. Monitor outbound network traffic for connections to unfamiliar or untrusted destinations. Ensure all Nexus Repository Manager instances are upgraded to version 3.15 or later to eliminate the vulnerability.
